## Hybrid Retrieval

**Hybrid retrieval** combines sparse lexical search (e.g. BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the two ranked result sets to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity.[^1]

### Ranking Fusion

Results from the two search methods are merged using techniques such as **reciprocal rank fusion**, which reweights and combines rankings from independent retrieval systems into a single ranked list.

### Use Cases

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone on queries that mix:
- Rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs)
- Natural language intent

This makes it particularly valuable when a search query combines domain-specific jargon or system references with free-text intent.

### Production Status

Hybrid retrieval has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems.[^1]

## Citations
